intro: Forget the idea of a single palace. Yıldız Palace, in İstanbul province, is a 19th-century palace town: a scatter of pavilions spread through a wooded park, from which Abdülhamid II governed for thirty-three years.
history: In 1877 Abdülhamid II moved the court from Dolmabahçe to Yıldız, and he governed from here for thirty-three years. It is not one palace but a compound of pavilions, workshops, a theatre, a carpentry shop and greenhouses, scattered through a wooded park. And in his spare hours? The sultan was here, at the workbench.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Şale pavilion and the Yıldız theatre. Visit the porcelain factory, and look for the Malta and Çadır pavilions.
facts: Did you know? The porcelain factory in the palace grounds was an attempt to set up home production against European imports, and it is still working. Abdülhamid II governed from here for thirty-three years, and the palace is not one building but a whole compound scattered through a park.
outro: This brings our visit to Yıldız Palace to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Let these pavilions keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
